stopped_cell.goal: What events do I have the Wednesday after next in Simple Calendar Pro? Answer with the titles only. If there are multiple titles, format your answer as a comma separated list.

blocked_fourth_next_day_action.initial_error: LOOP_GUARD: the same coordinate action has already been executed three consecutive times.
blocked_fourth_next_day_action.repair_error: LOOP_GUARD: the same coordinate action has already been executed three consecutive times.

root_cause.summary: B3 resolved 'the Wednesday after next' as the first future Wednesday, then its stepwise recovery was rejected by the unchanged cross-state coordinate-streak guard and repeated unchanged in the sole repair.
details: The target instance and paired hashes were unchanged; this was not task-instance drift.
The model first selected October 18 instead of October 25.
Both premature answers were correctly rejected by the same-turn critic and text-source guard.
The policy then advanced October 18 to October 21 with three semantically effective taps on the visible next-day arrow.
The fourth identical coordinate was correctly not executed under the frozen r33 guard.
The bounded repair repeated the same arrow and therefore failed validation without executing a blocked action.

r34_required_change.scope: Relative calendar-date grounding and bounded recovery from repeated stepwise navigation.
mechanism: Define the next named weekday as the first strictly future occurrence and that weekday after next as the following occurrence; when today is that weekday, use +7 and +14 days.
Prefer direct target selection with a visible month grid or date picker and verify the visible absolute date before answering.
Keep the three-action identical-coordinate cap unchanged.
When LOOP_GUARD rejects repeated navigation, require a materially different higher-level visible selector and forbid coordinate perturbation or repetition.
Run the exact frozen sequence 6 as a separate non-scored development reproduction before any fresh eight-cell formal suite.
prohibited: Changing the task seed, schedule, evaluator, budgets, or acceptance thresholds
Leaking task parameters or evaluator state to the policy
Weakening or removing the existing loop threshold
